correctness.rationale: For each positive diagonal \(d_j\), a Gram factorization yields \(R_j=A-Ae_je_j^{\mathsf T}A/d_j\succeq0\), with rank one less than \(A\), so \(r_j=\operatorname{tr}R_j>0\). With \(T=\sum_jd_j\) and \(Q=\sum_jd_j^q\), the change-of-measure bound and Hölder give \(\mathcal E_q/\mathcal E_1\le T(\max_jd_j)^{q-1}/Q\le n^{1-1/q}\) for every real \(q>1\). For \(\operatorname{diag}(t,J_m)\), pivoting the singleton leaves trace \(m\) and pivoting the large block leaves trace \(t\); the two event weights are \(t^q/(t^q+m)\) and \(m/(t^q+m)\). Substitution gives exactly \((\mathcal E_q/\mathcal E_1)-1=(m-t)(t^{q-1}-1)/(2(t^q+m))\), determining the entire equality/strict sign region. Taking \(t=((q-1)m)^{1/q}\) gives the asserted nonzero constant times \(m^{1-1/q}\) asymptotically. For the two-block squared-diagonal rule, differentiating \(F=(rt+s)(t+1)/(2(rt^2+s))\) gives \(F\prime=(r+s)(s-rt^2)/(2(rt^2+s)^2)\), whose unique maximum is \(1/2+n/(4\sqrt{rs})\), globally largest when \(rs=n-1\). The SPD extension follows from continuity of all positive-diagonal expected risks. The actual packaged checker passed 2137 exact-rational checks, which support calculations but cannot prove the continuous-parameter or infinite-family cases.

originality.rationale: Chen et al. define the exact Gibbs law and establish \(q=1\) trace bounds and infinite-power greedy counterexamples; Steinerberger proves a \(q=2\) Frobenius bound and already observes a small empirical trace reversal. Neither inspected primary full text provides the new finite-exponent \(\Theta(n^{1-1/q})\) first-pivot expected trace-error ratio, its exact two-block sign region, or the squared-rule restricted-class optimum. Other published results were compared by mathematical implication rather than title, including a statement about squared Frobenius error in the same block family, which does not imply the present trace comparison. Novelty beyond these searches remains conditional on uncatalogued or alternative-terminology literature, and independently certified priority is not asserted.

value.rationale: The power-diagonal pivot laws and their different norm motivations appear in the inspected 2022 and 2024 primary sources. A published empirical trace reversal gives no sharp quantitative bound. The new theorem shows that for every fixed finite \(q>1\), the nuclear-norm cost of using this power rule instead of the standard \(q=1\) rule can grow as \(\Theta(n^{1-1/q})\), and proves no worse dimension exponent is possible. The natural orthogonal two-block rank-two family yields an exact sign frontier and a restricted-class squared-diagonal optimum, including an exact 17-coordinate witness. This quantifies a concrete numerical-method choice and structural worst-case boundary rather than relabeling a method or recomputing a known table; no claim is made about later adaptive pivots or Frobenius loss.
